source: Author requested six more Biological resources, October 15, 2026. These are new fauna-material brainstorming proposals governed by Docs/WORLD_BASIS.md; specific species, anatomy, yields and manufacturing uses are not established canon.
boundary: Raw harvested resources only. No ordinary meat/fat anatomy, general edibility, wood, cloth, natural free water, recipes or implemented harvesting is introduced. Catalog IDs do not create world objects, streaming, unload/reload state or persisted gameplay deltas.

defaults.Carrier metadata: Physical harvested cargo; container, packing, mass and handling policy unresolved.
defaults.Acquisition: Recover from a selected fauna species; anatomy, source availability and collection method remain proposals.
defaults.Crafting / processing: Inspect, segregate and qualify raw feed before selecting a later preparation route. No processing recipe, yield or performance established.
defaults.Limitations: Potentially contaminated faunal material. No food, drinking, medical, protective or functional suitability established; preparation and safe containment require design.
defaults.Classification basis: Author-invited biological-resource expansion. Anatomically distinct raw feeds rather than finished tools, processing agents or general edible fauna.
defaults.Tier basis: T0 as harvested, before inspection and preparation establish craft-ready T1 material. Potential use does not establish suitability or a recipe.

items.name: Faunal tracheal tubes
items.purpose: Hollow, ring-supported airway structures proposed as raw feed for short protective conduits or small passages after cleaning and qualification. Distinct from flat breathing-filter plates and antenna sheaths; no useful flow rate or pressure rating established.
items.icon: Several short pale-brown hollow tubes with visible reinforcing rings and broken branching ends.

fields.Search aliases: tracheal tubes; ringed airway tubes; raw biological conduits
fields.Acquisition: Recover intact ring-supported airway sections from a proposed insectoid fauna source; species and extraction method unresolved.
fields.Limitations: Fragility, internal contamination, dimensions and compatibility remain unknown. Not a breathing aid, certified filter, pressure hose or finished canister line.

items.name: Faunal gut-lining sacs
items.purpose: Flexible lining structures proposed as membrane feed for experimental industrial vessel liners or replaceable internal barriers. Distinct from joint membrane and raw hide; any chemical-service use requires compatibility testing and a separate fitted design.
items.icon: Two collapsed translucent amber sacs with uneven folded rims, shown as raw unattached tissue.

fields.Search aliases: gut lining; digestive membrane sacs; biological liner feed
fields.Limitations: Internal residues may be toxic. Recovery does not guarantee chemical resistance, a leakproof container, safe food contact or a finished seal. Species, stabilization and service life unresolved.

items.name: Faunal pigment nodules
items.purpose: Localized color-bearing deposits proposed as raw pigment feed for coatings, paper marking or decorative inlay trials. These solid deposits are separate from mineral-rich ichor and the existing prepared shell-pigment suspension.
items.icon: Several irregular ochre, dark red and charcoal nodules with fractured colored interiors.

fields.Search aliases: pigment bodies; faunal color deposits; raw biological pigment
fields.Acquisition: Recover localized color-bearing deposits from a selected fauna integument; species, deposit structure and useful yield remain proposals.
fields.Limitations: Color stability, toxicity, particle preparation and binder compatibility are unverified. No dye, paint, cosmetic or food coloring is supplied as harvested.

items.name: Faunal spring arches
items.purpose: Curved resilient cuticle structures proposed as raw feed for small spring elements, flexing catches or vibration-isolating spacers. Selected for possible elastic response rather than the straight pivot geometry of mineralized hinge rods or structural wing ribs.
items.icon: Three compact dark cuticle arches with thickened ends and a smooth bowed middle.

fields.Search aliases: resilient cuticle arches; biological spring blanks; flexure feed
fields.Acquisition: Recover bowed cuticle structures from a proposed spring-loaded fauna joint; source anatomy and extraction remain speculative.
fields.Limitations: Elastic recovery, fatigue, brittleness after drying and load limits are unknown. Not an installed spring, guaranteed shock absorber or source of stored electricity.

items.name: Faunal balance stones
items.purpose: Small dense nodules from proposed balance-sensing structures, considered as raw bead blanks, tiny counterweight feed or decorative inserts. Distinct from digestive grinding grit: these are individually recovered nodules rather than bulk abrasive granules.
items.icon: A few smooth pale oval nodules beside a split mineralized bead showing faint concentric layers.

fields.Search aliases: balance nodules; statolith-like stones; faunal bead blanks
fields.Acquisition: Recover individual mineralized nodules from a proposed sensory balance structure in selected fauna; anatomy and occurrence unresolved.
fields.Limitations: Size, density consistency, workability and useful yield unknown. No gemstone value, precision bearing quality or sensory power is granted to harvested nodules.

items.name: Faunal grooming-comb plates
items.purpose: Fine-toothed hard plates from proposed grooming limbs, considered as blanks for small cleaning combs, fiber-separating tools or scraper inserts. The raw plate differs from loose sensory bristles, gripping-pad scales and the finished household shell comb.
items.icon: Two narrow chitin plates with closely spaced integral teeth, one retaining a rough attachment edge.

fields.Search aliases: grooming lamellae; toothed faunal plates; raw chitin combs
fields.Acquisition: Recover intact toothed plates from a proposed grooming limb or shed appendage; source species and recovery method unresolved.
fields.Limitations: Tooth spacing, wear, contamination and grip mounting require qualification. Not a finished brush, certified filter or proof of effortless husk-fiber separation.
